title: Private information and bank‐loan pricing: The effect of upcoming corporate spinoffs

rival_explanations: the pre-spinoff spread effect reflects fundamental (time-invariant) characteristics of spinoff firms rather than banks' access to private information about the upcoming spinoff
reverse causality and correlated omitted variables drive the pre-spinoff loan-spread effect

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (US borrowing firms across two-digit SIC industries; concentration in the manufacturing sector, SIC 2000-3999; financial services firms excluded)
context.sample_size: 50,619 loan facilities (of which 259 in the 365-day pre-spinoff period)

analyses.label: Table 5, Columns 1-2 (main effect; Final Sample, lead lender FE)
analyses.sample: Final Sample, 50,619 loan facilities of US firms, 1986-2017

dv.name: Spread
dv.measure: Spread (loan interest-rate spread; unstandardized mean 224.95, SD 147.63 basis points outside the 1-year pre-spinoff period)

key_ivs.name: PreSpinoff1Year
key_ivs.measure: indicator = 1 for loan facilities provided in the 365-day (1-year) period before a spinoff public announcement

key_ivs.name: PreSpinoff1YearHighRisk
key_ivs.measure: PreSpinoff1Year loans to high-risk spinoff firms: parent experiences a post-spinoff decrease in Altman's Z-score more than the 75th percentile of yearly decreases within its two-digit SIC code

key_ivs.name: PreSpinoff1YearNon-HighRisk
key_ivs.measure: PreSpinoff1Year loans to spinoff firms not classified as high-risk

controls.name: Facility Amount (ln of loan facility amount)
Maturity (ln of loan maturity in months)
